items.title: Judge declines to dismiss Suno publicity rights case, as sixteen more musicians join the legal battle
items.excerpt: The judge in the Isbell-led right-of-publicity class action against Suno has denied Suno's motion to dismiss the original lawsuit, days after an amended complaint added 16 plaintiffs. This is the court ruling the planner flagged as the only valid Isbell v Suno follow-up.

history_match.title: The Chicks join Jason Isbell's class action against Suno, as amended complaint adds 16 plaintiffs and targets v6

items.title: Cyanite launches its conversational Concierge for music search
items.excerpt: Cyanite, which has used AI to analyse and tag music catalogues for years, launched Cyanite Concierge, a conversational AI search layer for B2B catalogue search (sync, libraries, publishers). Article is paywalled, so only the teaser is readable.

items.title: FL Studio 2026.2 Update: New Plugins and Workflow Features
items.excerpt: Image-Line's FL Studio 2026.2 upgrades the Gopher AI workflow assistant so it can organise tracks, route the mixer, adjust levels and plugin parameters, and write Piano Roll content. Stem separation now isolates guitar and piano stems as well.

history_match.title: Pro Tools now features AI stem separation

items.title: UA Universe: A New Developer Platform and Community for LUNA
items.excerpt: Universal Audio's UA Universe (public beta) lets LUNA users build and share custom workflow add-ons by text-prompting AI coding assistants such as Claude Code and Codex. Add-on actions are logged in LUNA's undo history, and early tools include swipe-comping and Ableton Live session import.

items.title: The AI revolution is coming for your electronic instruments
items.excerpt: MusicRadar feature on AI-assisted firmware modding of hardware instruments ("300 nerds with Claude are going to outcompete any synth manufacturer"), with comment from Elektron and Akai on the opportunities and risks for instrument makers.

items.title: Australia's AI and copyright debate heats up after new report
items.excerpt: A report from the Australian parliament's Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence includes copyright recommendations for AI training, and music-industry tensions are rising over it. Same event as the CMU/ARIA item below; artists including Kate Bush and Grace Jones were also reported (Guardian, URL unresolved) urging the government not to legalise AI 'theft'.

history_match.title: ARIA and PPCA launch 'Not AI's to Take' campaign for permission-first AI copyright rules in Australia

items.title: Aussie MPs' new AI proposals "disguise" pro-big tech copyright reforms as "a favour to creators", says ARIA boss
items.excerpt: The Australian MPs' AI report talks about protecting creators but proposes copyright reforms that would give AI companies "certainty". ARIA says no reform is needed and accuses the MPs of "gaslighting". Same event as the Music Ally item; pick one.

history_match.title: Australian music industry rejects 'divide and conquer' proposal to give musicians exemption from AI scraping

items.title: Tidal has banned AI generated music from its platform. But can the industry agree where the line between AI-generated and AI-assisted should be drawn?
items.excerpt: Analysis of where to draw the line between AI-generated and AI-assisted music: Tidal will remove wholly AI tracks but still accept and monetise AI-assisted ones. Tidal is saturated (carded 11-25), so this only works as a fresh definitional angle.

history_match.title: Tidal Is the First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music

items.title: AI Companies Want Independent Music. This Time, They're Asking Permission.
items.excerpt: Hypebot analysis of Sonilo's opt-in AI training licence with Symphonic, which promises artists payment for AI training, plus the open questions on royalties, consent and creative control. The Sonilo deal itself was carded 11-19, so this is a follow-up opinion piece.

history_match.title: $11M-backed AI startup Sonilo, founded by TikTok veterans, inks licensing deal with Symphonic to train its model on opted-in indie recordings

items.title: GEORGE LYNCH Says He Was Recently Involved In Recording Sessions Based On Songs That Were Created Using A.I.
items.excerpt: Asked about Suno, Dokken/Lynch Mob guitarist George Lynch said he had recently been hired for session work playing solos on songs that were originally generated with AI. Off-list outlet, included because music sources were thin on Black Friday.

items.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users "DJ their art"
items.excerpt: MIT CSAIL's TangiMap uses an AI agent to reprogram mixers and control pads, mapping digital widgets onto physical knobs, buttons and sliders for musical performance and other creative software. Off-list (research), included for supply.

items.title: Music Similarity Estimation from Jukebox Embeddings
items.excerpt: JukeSim estimates content-based music similarity from embeddings of the Jukebox generative music model, for cold-start recommendation. It performs on par with a learned baseline and beats hand-designed approaches.

history_match.title: Can Music Generation Models Tap Along? Evaluating Generative Approaches to Beat Tracking

items.title: MADlibs: Analyzing the Distribution of Generative Music
items.excerpt: MADlibs measures what text-to-music models will actually produce across the prompt space (their expressive support), using NLP-generated prompts and MIR analysis of the outputs. The stakes are framed for creators and musical culture.

items.title: Line-Level Singer Diarization in Multi-Member Pop Songs: A Benchmark, Lead-Vocal Isolation, and Song-Level Decoding
items.excerpt: Releases ColorCoded-SD, a benchmark of 43 K-pop songs with 3-8 singers each, for working out which member sings each lyric line. Commercial diarizers find only one or two speakers in these songs, and the paper proposes lead-vocal isolation and song-level decoding.
